proofs.proof_tex:
By \(\texttt{ass:fixed-lti-response}\), \(\texttt{ass:zero-prehistory}\), and \(\texttt{def:response-matrix}\), the observed vector is
\[
Y(X)=A(X)g+e.
\]
All denominators in \(\Gamma_T^{-1}\) are positive because \(0\leq \ell<K\leq T/2\).  Hence \(\texttt{def:causal-moment-estimator}\) and \(\texttt{def:error-components}\) give, equation by equation,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\widehat\tau-\tau
 &=q^{\top}\Gamma_T^{-1}A(X)^{\top}(A(X)g+e)-q^{\top}g\\
 &=\bigl(A(X)^{\top}A(X)\Gamma_T^{-1}q-q\bigr)^{\top}g
   +\bigl(A(X)\Gamma_T^{-1}q\bigr)^{\top}e\\
 &=u_T(X)^{\top}g+v_T(X)^{\top}e.
\end{aligned}
\]
For \(0\leq \ell,j<K\), pairwise orthogonality in \(\texttt{def:finite-design-class}\), together with \(X_s^2=1\) for \(s\geq1\) and zero prehistory, yields
\[
\mathbb E_D[(A^{\top}A)_{\ell j}]
=\begin{cases}T-\ell,&\ell=j,\\0,&\ell\ne j,
\end{cases}
\qquad\text{and therefore}\qquad
\mathbb E_D[A^{\top}A]=\Gamma_T.
\]
Thus \(\mathbb E_D[u_T]=0\).  Global sign symmetry in the same definition makes every odd function of \(X\) have expectation zero.  Since \(u_T(-X)=u_T(X)\) while \(v_T(-X)=-v_T(X)\),
\[
\mathbb E_D[u_Tv_T^{\top}]
=\frac12\mathbb E_D\!left[u_T(X)v_T(X)^{\top}+u_T(-X)v_T(-X)^{\top}\right]=0.
\]
The displayed entries in \(\texttt{def:error-components}\) give \(v_T=F_{T,q}X\).  Pairwise orthogonality and the binary diagonal give \(\mathbb E_D[XX^{\top}]=I_T\), whence
\[
\mathbb E_D[v_Tv_T^{\top}]=F_{T,q}\mathbb E_D[XX^{\top}]F_{T,q}^{\top}
=F_{T,q}F_{T,q}^{\top}.
\]
The fixed-path condition \(\texttt{ass:fixed-potential-path}\) ensures that these expectations are only over the assignment.  Put \(U_D=\mathbb E_D[u_Tu_T^{\top}]\).  The preceding cross-block identity gives
\[
\mathbb E_D[(\widehat\tau-\tau)^2]
=g^{\top}U_Dg+e^{\top}F_{T,q}F_{T,q}^{\top}e.
\]
Under the joint ellipsoid in \(\texttt{def:nuisance-class}\), write \(g=R_ga\) and \(e=\sqrt{T}R_eb\).  The constraint is \(\|a\|_2^2+\|b\|_2^2\leq1\).  The supremum of the last quadratic form is therefore the largest eigenvalue of the block-diagonal matrix
\[
\operatorname{Diag}\!left(R_g^2U_D,\,TR_e^2F_{T,q}F_{T,q}^{\top}\right),
\]
namely
\[
\max\!left\{R_g^2\lambda_{\max}(U_D),\,TR_e^2\|F_{T,q}\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2\right\}.
\]
Multiplication by \(T\), as required by \(\texttt{def:minimax-risk}\), proves
\[
\mathcal R_T(D)=\max\!left\{TR_g^2\lambda_{\max}(\mathbb E_D[u_Tu_T^{\top}]),\,
T^2R_e^2\|F_{T,q}\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2\right\}.
\]

Let \(n=T-1\) and use the edge variables in \(\texttt{def:mirrored-edge-law}\).  The independent fair sign \(X_1\) implies that replacing \(X_1\) by \(-X_1\), while keeping all edges fixed, replaces the entire path \(X\) by \(-X\).  Thus the resulting law has the global sign symmetry required by \(\texttt{def:finite-design-class}\).

We next show that every nonempty consecutive edge product is centered.  If such an interval lies wholly in an outer half of the displayed edge vector, it is a product of distinct independent \(A_i\)'s, up to a deterministic sign, and hence has mean zero.  If it meets but does not cross the center, it contains at least one of the independent central signs exactly once.  If it crosses the center, then for even \(T\) it contains \(B\) exactly once, while for odd \(T\) it contains both \(B\) and \(C\) exactly once.  In every case an independent fair factor occurs to the first power, so
\[
\mathbb E\!\left[\prod_{i=s}^{t-1}Z_i\right]=0
\qquad(1\leq s<t\leq T).
\]
Because the recursion \(X_{i+1}=X_iZ_i\) gives
\[
X_sX_t=\prod_{i=s}^{t-1}Z_i,
\]
all off-diagonal path moments vanish.  Hence \(D_T^{\mathrm{mir}}\in\mathfrak D_T\).

If \(T\) is even, the paired outer signs cancel in the edge sum and \(S_T=B\), so \(\mathbb E[S_T^2]=1=a_T\).  If \(T\) is odd, \(S_T=B+C\), so independence gives \(\mathbb E[S_T^2]=2=a_T\).

It remains to prove the pointwise dual certificates.  When \(T\) is even, \(n\) is odd, so the sum of the \(n\) signs \(Z_i\) is an odd integer.  Consequently
\[
S_T^2\geq1.
\]
When \(T\) is odd, \(n\) is even.  Define
\[
c=(-1)^{n/2},\qquad \chi=\prod_{i=1}^{n}Z_i=X_1X_T.
\]
If \(k\) edges are negative, then \(S_T=n-2k\) and \(\chi=(-1)^k\), hence
\[
c\chi=(-1)^{n/2-k}=(-1)^{S_T/2}.
\]
If \(c\chi=1\), then \(S_T\) is divisible by \(4\) and \(S_T^2\geq0\); if \(c\chi=-1\), then \(S_T\equiv2\pmod4\) and \(S_T^2\geq4\).  These two cases are exactly
\[
S_T^2\geq2-2(-1)^{(T-1)/2}X_1X_T.
\]
For the prescribed \(T=5\) check this reads \(S_5^2\geq2-2X_1X_5\), while the mirrored edges are \((A_1,B,C,-A_1)\) and \(S_5=B+C\), which takes \(-2,0,2\) with probabilities \(1/4,1/2,1/4\).  Thus its second moment is exactly \(2\), confirming the parity certificate at the smallest odd horizon.

Assume \(K=2\) and \(q=(1,0)^{\top}\).  By \(\texttt{def:response-matrix}\) and \(\texttt{def:error-components}\), the first column of \(A\) is \(X\), the off-diagonal entry of \(A^{\top}A\) is \(S_T\), and \(\Gamma_T^{-1}q=(1/T,0)^{\top}\).  Therefore
\[
u_T(X)=\begin{pmatrix}0\\S_T(X)/T\end{pmatrix},
\qquad v_T(X)=X/T,
\qquad F_{T,q}=I_T/T.
\]
Applying \(\texttt{lem:exact-risk-reduction}\) gives, for every \(D\in\mathfrak D_T\),
\[
\mathcal R_T(D)
=\max\!\left\{R_e^2,\frac{R_g^2}{T}\mathbb E_D[S_T^2]\right\}.
\tag{1}
\]
The pointwise certificates in \(\texttt{lem:mirrored-law-membership}\), and pairwise orthogonality \(\mathbb E_D[X_1X_T]=0\) in the odd case, imply
\[
\mathbb E_D[S_T^2]\geq a_T
\qquad\text{for every }D\in\mathfrak D_T.
\tag{2}
\]
The mirrored law belongs to \(\mathfrak D_T\) and has equality in (2).  Taking the infimum of (1) therefore proves the matching lower and upper bounds
\[
V_{T,2}(q;R_g,R_e)=\max\!\left\{R_e^2,\frac{a_TR_g^2}{T}\right\}.
\tag{3}
\]

By \(\texttt{def:lag-one-objects}\), \(r_T=TR_e^2/R_g^2\), which is well defined because both radii are positive.  Comparing (1) and (3), a feasible law is minimax exactly when
\[
\max\{r_T,\mathbb E_D[S_T^2]\}=\max\{r_T,a_T\}.
\]
Together with (2), this is equivalent to
\[
\mathbb E_D[S_T^2]\leq\max\{a_T,r_T\}.
\]
If \(r_T\leq a_T\), (2) forces equality \(\mathbb E_D[S_T^2]=a_T\).  In the even case, the nonnegative pointwise slack \(S_T^2-1\) has expectation zero exactly when \(S_T^2=1\) almost surely, or equivalently the law is supported on \(S_T\in\{-1,1\}\).  In the odd case, equality in the expected certificate requires equality in its pointwise form almost surely; the parity analysis in \(\texttt{lem:mirrored-law-membership}\) shows that this occurs exactly for \(S_T\in\{-2,0,2\}\).  Conversely any legal law with the corresponding support has second moment \(a_T\), so these conditions are also sufficient.  This proves the complete optimizer face and its primal and parity-dual certificates.

Under \(\texttt{def:iid-law}\), the path is uniform on \(\{-1,+1\}^T\).  It is invariant under global sign reversal and has zero off-diagonal second moments, so \(D_T^{\mathrm{iid}}\in\mathfrak D_T\) by \(\texttt{def:finite-design-class}\).  The map
\[
(X_1,\ldots,X_T)\longmapsto(X_1,Z_1,\ldots,Z_{T-1}),
\qquad Z_t=X_tX_{t+1},
\]
is a bijection of the binary cube.  Hence under the uniform law the variables \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_{T-1}\) are independent fair signs.  Thus
\[
\mathbb E_{D_T^{\mathrm{iid}}}[S_T^2]
=\sum_{t=1}^{T-1}\mathbb E[Z_t^2]
  +2\sum_{s<t}\mathbb E[Z_s]\mathbb E[Z_t]
=T-1.
\]
Equation (1) in \(\texttt{thm:lag-one-minimax}\) now yields
\[
\mathcal R_T(D_T^{\mathrm{iid}})
=\max\!\left\{R_e^2,\frac{(T-1)R_g^2}{T}\right\}.
\]
Since \(T\geq4\) implies \(T-1>a_T\), comparison with the minimax value in that theorem shows equality if and only if
\[
R_e^2\geq\frac{T-1}{T}R_g^2.
\]
Below this threshold, the independent-law risk is its signal term, and subtraction of the minimax value gives
\[
\frac{(T-1)R_g^2}{T}
-\max\!\left\{R_e^2,\frac{a_TR_g^2}{T}\right\}>0,
\]
as claimed.

Let \(D\in\mathfrak D_T^{\mathrm{RS}}\cap\mathfrak D_T\).  If \(\rho_{\mathrm{RS}}+\gamma_{\mathrm{RS}}>0\), stationarity in \(\texttt{ass:stationary-random-switch-law}\) gives
\[
\Pr_D(X_t=1)=\frac{\rho_{\mathrm{RS}}}{\rho_{\mathrm{RS}}+\gamma_{\mathrm{RS}}}.
\]
Global sign symmetry from \(\mathfrak D_T\) makes this probability \(1/2\), so
\(\rho_{\mathrm{RS}}=\gamma_{\mathrm{RS}}=:p\).  The one-step product then satisfies
\[
\mathbb E_D[X_tX_{t+1}]
=\Pr_D(X_{t+1}=X_t)-\Pr_D(X_{t+1}\ne X_t)=1-2p.
\]
Pairwise orthogonality forces this quantity to zero, hence \(p=1/2\).  The transition matrix then has both rows \((1/2,1/2)\), so the path law is \(D_T^{\mathrm{iid}}\).  If instead \(\rho_{\mathrm{RS}}=\gamma_{\mathrm{RS}}=0\), the chain is constant and \(\mathbb E_D[X_tX_{t+1}]=1\), contradicting pairwise orthogonality.  Conversely the independent Rademacher law is the stationary random-switch law with both transition probabilities equal to \(1/2\), and it belongs to \(\mathfrak D_T\).  Therefore
\[
\mathfrak D_T^{\mathrm{RS}}\cap\mathfrak D_T=\{D_T^{\mathrm{iid}}\}.
\]

By \(\texttt{lem:mirrored-law-membership}\), \(D_T^{\mathrm{mir}}\in\mathfrak D_T\), while
\[
\mathbb E_{D_T^{\mathrm{mir}}}[S_T^2]=a_T<T-1
=\mathbb E_{D_T^{\mathrm{iid}}}[S_T^2].
\]
Thus the two laws differ, so the intersection is a strict subset of \(\mathfrak D_T\) and \(D_T^{\mathrm{mir}}\notin\mathfrak D_T^{\mathrm{RS}}\).  Finally, if \(R_e^2/R_g^2<(T-1)/T\), \(\texttt{prop:iid-optimality-threshold}\) says that the only law in the intersection is not minimax, while \(\texttt{thm:lag-one-minimax}\) and \(\texttt{lem:mirrored-law-membership}\) say that the mirrored law is minimax.  Every comparison here is of \(\mathcal R_T\), the fixed-path worst-case mean squared error of the displayed moment estimator; no equality with an asymptotic least-squares information criterion is used.

First consider one block in \(\texttt{def:golay-block-law}\).  For a multiset \(J=(j_1,\ldots,j_m)\), direct multiplication gives
\[
\prod_{r=1}^{m}W_{j_r}
=\sigma^m(-1)^{\sum_{r=1}^{m}\phi_L(j_r)}
 (-1)^{\alpha\cdot(\bigoplus_{r=1}^{m}j_r)}.
\tag{4}
\]
The average over the fair sign \(\sigma\) is zero when \(m\) is odd.  When \(m\) is even, orthogonality of the characters of \(\mathbb F_2^p\) gives
\[
2^{-p}\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbb F_2^p}(-1)^{\alpha\cdot h}
=\mathbf1\{h=0\}.
\]
Applying this identity to (4) proves exactly the coefficient \(\kappa_L(J)\) in \(\texttt{def:fourth-tensor-certificate}\).

Condition on the uniform block phase.  Indices in different blocks involve independent block parameters, so their joint moment factors over blocks; within each block the factor is the just-computed \(\kappa_L\).  Averaging over the \(L\) phases proves
\[
\mathbb E[X_{t_1}^{\infty}X_{t_2}^{\infty}X_{t_3}^{\infty}X_{t_4}^{\infty}]
=\Theta_L(t_1,t_2,t_3,t_4).
\]
The same calculation with one index gives mean zero.  With two distinct indices, either they lie in different blocks and centeredness applies, or they lie in one block and their binary labels have nonzero xor, so the character average is zero.  Since every square is one,
\[
\mathbb E[X_s^{\infty}X_t^{\infty}]=\mathbf1\{s=t\}.
\]

We next establish the autocorrelation bound without importing it as a hypothesis.  Suppress the irrelevant global sign.  For a length \(2^r\) affine word \(P_r\), define \(Q_r(j)=(-1)^{j_{r-1}}P_r(j)\).  Splitting on the highest bit gives, for a sign \(\varepsilon\) determined by the corresponding affine coefficient,
\[
P_r=(P_{r-1},\varepsilon Q_{r-1}),
\qquad Q_r=(P_{r-1},-\varepsilon Q_{r-1}).
\tag{5}
\]
At length two the aperiodic autocorrelations of \(P_1\) and \(Q_1\) cancel.  If the two words at level \(r-1\) have cancelling autocorrelations at every positive lag, then (5) shows the same at level \(r\): below the half-length the two within-half sums add to twice the preceding complementary sum while the two crossing sums cancel, and at or above the half-length only the crossing sums remain and cancel.  Induction therefore proves
\[
C_{P_r,h}+C_{Q_r,h}=0\qquad(1\leq h<2^r).
\tag{6}
\]
For the single length-\(L\) word \(W=(P_{p-1},\varepsilon Q_{p-1})\), a shift \(h<L/2\) has two within-half contributions, which cancel by (6), and exactly \(h\) crossing products.  Hence \(|C_{L,h}(W)|\leq h\).  At \(h=L/2\) there are only \(h\) crossing products, so the same bound holds there as well.  In particular, it applies for every \(1\leq h\leq d\) whenever \(L\geq2d\), and the displayed strict-range assertion follows.

Because \(M_L\) is the second moment matrix of the lag-sum vector,
\[
\operatorname{tr}(M_L+H_d)
=\sum_{h=1}^{d}\bigl(\mathbb E[C_{L,h}(W)^2]+h\bigr)
\leq\sum_{h=1}^{d}(h^2+h).
\tag{7}
\]

For the covariance limit, first align a window with \(B\) complete blocks.  Let \(I_b=C_L(W^{(b)})\), and for the boundary from block \(b\) to block \(b+1\) put
\[
J_{b,h}=\sum_{i=0}^{h-1}W^{(b)}_{L-h+i}W^{(b+1)}_i,
\qquad 1\leq h\leq d.
\]
Pairwise orthogonality within a block gives \(\mathbb E[I_b]=0\) and
\[
\mathbb E[J_{b,h}J_{b,k}]
=\sum_{i=0}^{h-1}\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}
 \mathbb E[W^{(b)}_{L-h+i}W^{(b)}_{L-k+j}]
 \mathbb E[W^{(b+1)}_iW^{(b+1)}_j]
=h\mathbf1\{h=k\}.
\tag{8}
\]
Thus \(\mathbb E[J_bJ_b^{\top}]=H_d\).  Different internal vectors are independent.  An internal--boundary product contains a single centered factor from the other block, and a product of boundary vectors at different boundaries contains a single centered factor from an outer block (unless the boundaries coincide).  Hence all such cross-covariances vanish.  The exact aligned identity is consequently
\[
\mathbb E[C_{BL}(X^{\infty})C_{BL}(X^{\infty})^{\top}]
=BM_L+(B-1)H_d.
\tag{9}
\]
A general random-phase window differs from an aligned union of complete blocks by at most two partial blocks and a fixed number, depending only on \(L,d\), of crossing products.  Its remainder is deterministically bounded for fixed \(L,d\); (9) and Cauchy--Schwarz show that its covariance contribution divided by \(T\) vanishes.  Since \(B/T\to1/L\),
\[
T^{-1}\mathbb E[C_T(X^{\infty})C_T(X^{\infty})^{\top}]
\longrightarrow\frac{M_L+H_d}{L}.
\]

For the requested finite checks, direct substitution of all affine masks at both \(L=8\) and \(L=16\) gives the four values
\[
(C_1,C_2,C_3,C_4)\in
\{(-1,0,-1,0),\,(-1,0,3,0),\,(1,0,-3,0),\,(1,0,1,0)\}
\]
with equal multiplicities (respectively two and four masks, before the duplicate global signs).  Hence, for both lengths,
\[
M_L\big|_{d=3}=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&-1\\0&0&0\\-1&0&5\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
(M_L+H_3)=\begin{pmatrix}2&0&-1\\0&2&0\\-1&0&8\end{pmatrix}.
\]
For \(d=2\) the leading blocks are \(M_L=\operatorname{Diag}(1,0)\) and \(M_L+H_2=2I_2\).  These enumerations agree with (7)--(9) and verify the endpoint normalization for \(K=3,4\).

Fix \(K,q\), and write \(C_h=C_{T,h}(X)\).  For \(0\leq \ell,j<K\), direct use of the zero-prehistory convention in \(\texttt{ass:zero-prehistory}\) gives
\[
(A^{\top}A)_{\ell j}
=\begin{cases}
T-\ell,&j=\ell,\\
C_{|\ell-j|}-E_{\ell j,T},&j\ne\ell,
\end{cases}
\tag{10}
\]
where \(E_{\ell j,T}\) is the terminal sum omitted by the shorter lagged column and contains exactly \(\min(\ell,j)\) binary products.  Thus \(|E_{\ell j,T}|\leq\min(\ell,j)\).  The diagonal contribution to \(A^{\top}A\Gamma_T^{-1}q-q\) cancels exactly.  Grouping the off-diagonal terms in (10) by \(h=|\ell-j|\) yields
\[
u_{T,\ell}
=\frac1T\sum_{h=1}^{d}
\left(q_{\ell-h}\mathbf1\{\ell\geq h\}
+q_{\ell+h}\mathbf1\{\ell+h<K\}\right)C_h+\rho_{T,\ell},
\tag{11}
\]
where every summand of the remainder is of the form
\[
q_j\left[\left(\frac1{T-j}-\frac1T\right)C_{|\ell-j|}
-\frac{E_{\ell j,T}}{T-j}\right].
\]
Since \(|C_h|\leq T-h\), \(|E_{\ell j,T}|\leq K\), and \(T-j\geq T-K+1\geq T/2\), there is a finite constant depending only on \(K,q\) such that
\[
\sup_X\|\rho_T(X)\|_2\leq \frac{c_{K,q}}{T}.
\tag{12}
\]
The coefficient in parentheses in (11) is precisely the entry of \(D_q\) from \(\texttt{def:block-covariance-objects}\), proving
\[
u_T(X)=T^{-1}D_qC_T(X)+\rho_T(X).
\]

Under \(D_L^{\mathrm G}\), \(\texttt{lem:golay-tensor-certificate}\) implies \(\mathbb E\|C_T\|_2^2=O_{L,d}(T)\).  From (12),
\[
T\mathbb E\|\rho_T\|_2^2=O(T^{-1})\to0,
\]
and Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
T\left\|\mathbb E\left[(T^{-1}D_qC_T)\rho_T^{\top}\right]\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\leq
T\bigl(\mathbb E\|T^{-1}D_qC_T\|_2^2\bigr)^{1/2}
 \bigl(\mathbb E\|\rho_T\|_2^2\bigr)^{1/2}
=O(T^{-1/2})\to0.
\]
This proves both asserted remainder negligibilities.

Finally, let \(S_\ell\) denote the lower shift by \(\ell\) coordinates on \(\mathbb R^T\).  Then
\[
TF_{T,q}=\sum_{\ell=0}^{d}\frac{Tq_\ell}{T-\ell}S_\ell.
\tag{13}
\]
This finite matrix is a compression of bilateral convolution with polynomial
\(Q_T(z)=\sum_{\ell=0}^{d}Tq_\ell z^\ell/(T-\ell)\).  Fourier diagonalization of bilateral convolution, proved by Parseval's identity, gives the upper bound
\[
\|TF_{T,q}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\leq\max_{|z|=1}|Q_T(z)|\longrightarrow N_q,
\tag{14}
\]
because the finitely many coefficients converge uniformly.  For the reverse bound, choose \(z_0\) maximizing \(|Q_q(z)|\) and use the normalized complex vector \(x_s=T^{-1/2}z_0^{-s}\).  On all but the first \(d\) output coordinates, (13) acts by multiplication by \(Q_T(z_0)\), up to an irrelevant unit-modulus factor.  Consequently
\[
\|TF_{T,q}\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2
\geq\frac{T-d}{T}|Q_T(z_0)|^2\longrightarrow N_q^2.
\tag{15}
\]
The operator norm of a real matrix is unchanged by complexification.  Equations (14)--(15) prove \(T\|F_{T,q}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\to N_q\).

We first verify feasibility and finite-state complexity.  The random uniform phase in \(\texttt{def:golay-block-law}\) makes \(D_L^{\mathrm G}\) invariant under a unit shift.  The one- and two-point calculations in \(\texttt{lem:golay-tensor-certificate}\) give global sign symmetry and zero off-origin autocorrelation, so \(D_L^{\mathrm G}\in\mathfrak D_\infty\) by \(\texttt{def:stationary-design-class}\).  More explicitly, global negation corresponds to replacing every independent block sign by its negative, which preserves their joint law.  A hidden state may be taken as
\[
(r,\alpha,\sigma)\in\{0,\ldots,L-1\}\times\mathbb F_2^p\times\{-1,+1\}.
\]
For \(r<L-1\) the phase advances deterministically, and at \(r=L-1\) a fresh independent uniform \((\alpha,\sigma)\) is drawn and the phase returns to zero.  The uniform distribution on these \(2L^2\) states is invariant and emits exactly the random-phase block law, proving the asserted complexity bound.

For a fixed such \(L\), combine \(\texttt{lem:zero-prehistory-asymptotics}\) with the covariance limit in \(\texttt{lem:golay-tensor-certificate}\).  Continuity of the largest eigenvalue gives
\[
T\mathbb E[u_Tu_T^{\top}]
\longrightarrow \frac1L D_q(M_L+H_d)D_q^{\top}.
\tag{16}
\]
The same zero-prehistory lemma gives
\[
T^2\|F_{T,q}\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2\longrightarrow N_q^2.
\tag{17}
\]
Every finite restriction of the stationary law belongs to \(\mathfrak D_T\).  Hence \(\texttt{lem:exact-risk-reduction}\), (16), (17), and the definition of stationary risk imply the exact formula
\[
\mathcal R_{\infty,K}(D_L^{\mathrm G})
=\max\!\left\{R_e^2N_q^2,\frac{R_g^2}{L}
\lambda_{\max}\bigl(D_q(M_L+H_d)D_q^{\top}\bigr)\right\}.
\tag{18}
\]

We now certify when the second block cannot exceed the first.  From the definition of \(D_q\), the inequality \((a+b)^2\leq2a^2+2b^2\), and a count over the two possible shifts,
\[
\|D_q\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2\leq\|D_q\|_{\mathrm F}^2
\leq2\sum_{j=0}^{d}\bigl((d-j)+j\bigr)q_j^2
=2d\|q\|_2^2.
\tag{19}
\]
Parseval's identity gives
\[
\|q\|_2^2=\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}|Q_q(e^{i\omega})|^2\,d\omega
\leq N_q^2.
\tag{20}
\]
The autocorrelation estimate proved in \(\texttt{lem:golay-tensor-certificate}\) is valid also at \(d=L/2\), so for every \(L\geq2d\), equations (7), (19), and (20) yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
\lambda_{\max}\bigl(D_q(M_L+H_d)D_q^{\top}\bigr)
&\leq \|D_q\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2\operatorname{tr}(M_L+H_d)\\
&\leq2dN_q^2\sum_{h=1}^{d}(h^2+h)
=B_KN_q^2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{21}
\]
Thus if \(L\geq B_KR_g^2/R_e^2\), positivity of \(R_e\) and (21) show that the signal term in (18) is at most \(R_e^2N_q^2\).  Equation (18) then proves exact attainment of the noise floor.  This also covers \(q=0\), when both terms vanish.

It remains to prove that this floor is globally minimax and is the finite-horizon limit.  For every \(D\in\mathfrak D_T\), \(\texttt{lem:exact-risk-reduction}\) gives the design-independent lower bound
\[
\mathcal R_T(D)\geq T^2R_e^2\|F_{T,q}\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2.
\]
Taking the infimum and using (17) yields
\[
\liminf_{T\to\infty}V_{T,K}(q;R_g,R_e)\geq R_e^2N_q^2.
\tag{22}
\]
Choose one power of two \(L\) satisfying the two displayed lower bounds in the theorem.  Its restriction is feasible for every \(T\), so
\[
V_{T,K}(q;R_g,R_e)\leq\mathcal R_T(D_L^{\mathrm G}|_{1:T}).
\]
The right side converges by (16)--(18) to \(R_e^2N_q^2\), proving the reverse \(\limsup\) inequality and hence
\[
\lim_{T\to\infty}V_{T,K}(q;R_g,R_e)=R_e^2N_q^2.
\tag{23}
\]
For any \(P_\infty\in\mathfrak D_\infty\), the same design-independent lower bound and (17) imply
\(\mathcal R_{\infty,K}(P_\infty)\geq R_e^2N_q^2\).  The chosen \(D_L^{\mathrm G}\) attains equality by (18)--(21).  Taking the stationary infimum proves
\[
V_{\infty,K}(q;R_g,R_e)=R_e^2N_q^2,
\]
which together with (23) establishes the stated equality of finite-horizon and stationary limits.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A lag-sized necessary-and-sufficient description of the genuine binary fourth-moment projection, with constructive sign-orbit recovery and a uniform finite-horizon rate certificate.
open_obligations.obstruction: Positivity of the lifted covariance and the parity inequalities used at one lag do not characterize the correlation polytope at general lag order. The exact orbit formulation remains exponential, and the stationary block argument by itself supplies a limit but not the requested uniform finite-horizon rate.
open_obligations.attempted: Reduced the feasible set to global-sign orbit weights, projected it through the exact quadratic-error map, checked the scalar parity collapse at one lag, and tested whether the Golay block covariance eliminates the finite-window boundary coordinates. The latter proves the stationary limit but does not furnish sign-orbit recovery for every feasible projected tensor.
open_obligations.partial_result:
A computable exact characterization is available at exponential, rather than lag-sized, scale.  Let \(\mathcal O_T\) be the set of global-sign orbits in \(\{-1,+1\}^T\), choose a representative \(x_o\) of each orbit, and let \(p_o\) be its total probability.  Then the relevant projected fourth-moment set is exactly
\[
\left\{
\sum_{o\in\mathcal O_T}p_o,u_T(x_o)u_T(x_o)^{\top}:
p_o\geq0,\quad \sum_op_o=1,\quad
\sum_op_o x_{o,s}x_{o,t}=0\ \text{for all }s<t
\right\}.
\]
Consequently \(V_{T,K}\) is computed exactly by minimizing
\[
\max\!\left\{TR_g^2\lambda_{\max}\!\left(\sum_op_o u_T(x_o)u_T(x_o)^{\top}\right),
T^2R_e^2\|F_{T,q}\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2\right\}
\]
over the displayed simplex and linear moment constraints; an epigraph variable turns this into a finite semidefinite program.  The lag-one parity proof collapses this program to one scalar moment, and the stationary Golay construction proves convergence of its value for fixed \(K,q\).  What is not proved is a necessary-and-sufficient description having size controlled only by the lag order, sign-orbit recovery from such a description, or the requested uniform finite-horizon \(T^{-1}\) error bound.

proofs.proof_tex:
Set \(T=4\).  By \(\text{def:mirrored-edge-law}\), \(m_4=1\), so if we write \(a=A_1\), \(b=B\), and \(s=X_1\), then \(a,b,s\) are mutually independent uniform signs and
\[
 (Z_1,Z_2,Z_3)=(a,b,-a).
\]
The recursion \(X_{t+1}=X_tZ_t\) in the same definition and the identity \(a^2=1\) give, successively,
\[
 X_1=s,\qquad X_2=sa,\qquad X_3=sab,\qquad X_4=(sab)(-a)=-sb.
\]
Thus
\[
 X=(s,sa,sab,-sb).
\]
Each triple \((a,b,s)\in\{-1,+1\}^3\) has probability \(2^{-3}=1/8\).  Substitution of the eight triples into the last display gives exactly the eight paths in \(\text{def:t4-mirrored-audit}\), including their displayed probabilities.

By \(\text{def:lag-one-objects}\) and the defining relation \(Z_t=X_tX_{t+1}\) from \(\text{def:mirrored-edge-law}\),
\[
 S_4=\sum_{t=1}^{3}X_tX_{t+1}=\sum_{t=1}^{3}Z_t=a+b-a=b=B.
\]
This equality is pointwise, hence holds in every row of the displayed table.  Because \(B\in\{-1,+1\}\), it also gives pointwise \(S_4^2=B^2=1\), and therefore
\[
 \mathbb E_{D_4^{\mathrm{mir}}}[S_4^2]=1.
\]

It remains to audit every off-diagonal entry of the second-moment matrix.  For \(1\le i<j\le4\), repeated use of \(X_{t+1}=X_tZ_t\) and \(X_i^2=1\) yields
\[
 X_iX_j=\prod_{r=i}^{j-1}Z_r.
\]
Since independent uniform signs have mean zero, the six off-diagonal expectations are
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E[X_1X_2]&=\mathbb E[a]=0,
 &\mathbb E[X_2X_3]&=\mathbb E[b]=0,
 &\mathbb E[X_3X_4]&=\mathbb E[-a]=0,\\
 \mathbb E[X_1X_3]&=\mathbb E[ab]=\mathbb E[a]\mathbb E[b]=0,
 &\mathbb E[X_2X_4]&=\mathbb E[-ab]=-\mathbb E[a]\mathbb E[b]=0,
 &\mathbb E[X_1X_4]&=\mathbb E[-a^2b]=-\mathbb E[b]=0.
\end{aligned}
\]
All four diagonal entries equal \(\mathbb E[X_i^2]=1\).  Symmetry of \(XX^{\top}\) now proves
\[
 \mathbb E_{D_4^{\mathrm{mir}}}[XX^{\top}]=I_4.
\]

Finally, holding \((a,b)\) fixed and replacing \(s\) by \(-s\) sends the formula \(X=(s,sa,sab,-sb)\) to \(-X\).  The two values of \(s\) have equal conditional probability, so for every \(B_0\subseteq\{-1,+1\}^4\),
\[
 D_4^{\mathrm{mir}}(B_0)=D_4^{\mathrm{mir}}(-B_0).
\]
Together with the already proved identities \(\mathbb E[X_iX_j]=0\) for every \(i<j\), the two membership conditions in \(\text{def:finite-design-class}\) give
\[
 D_4^{\mathrm{mir}}\in\mathfrak D_4.
\]
Moreover, \(T=4\) is even, so \(\text{def:lag-one-objects}\) gives \(a_4=1\); hence the pointwise calculation above reads \(\mathbb E[S_4^2]=1=a_4\), which is precisely the claimed finite audit of the even-horizon value.

proposed.statement: The displayed \(T=4\) table satisfies \(S_4=B\) row by row, \(\mathbb E_{D_4^{\mathrm{mir}}}[XX^{\top}]=I_4\), and \(\mathbb E_{D_4^{\mathrm{mir}}}[S_4^2]=1\); hence it gives a direct finite audit of \(D_4^{\mathrm{mir}}\in\mathfrak D_4\) and the even-horizon bound.
proposed.justification: The complete support table exposes every probability, path, edge sum, and pairwise-moment check in the smallest nontrivial horizon.
proposed.gap: Neither covariance relaxations nor independent-toggling calculations exhibit a correlated binary law whose full path-pair moment matrix and parity value can be inspected row by row.
proposed.consumer: It is a reproducible unit test for implementations of the mirrored randomizer and for the \(T=4\) parity certificate.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proof necessarily unfolds the existing definition of the lag-one sum and the parity value, so the statement's dependency metadata must include def:lag-one-objects; the mathematical claim itself is unchanged.

proofs.proof_tex:
Write (j=(j_0,j_1,j_2)inmathbb F_2^3) for the binary digits of (jin{0,ldots,7}), with (j_0) the least significant bit.  By the random-phase affine Boolean block construction in (mathrm{def{:}golay  ext{-}block  ext{-}law}), for any finite list (j_1,ldots,j_m) (repetitions allowed),
\[
 \prod_{r=1}^m W_{j_r}
 =\sigma^m(-1)^{\sum_{r=1}^m\phi_8(j_r)}
   \prod_{k=0}^2(-1)^{\alpha_k\sum_{r=1}^m(j_r)_k}.
\]
All exponents in the last product are read in (mathbb F_2).  The sign (sigma) and bits (alpha_0,alpha_1,alpha_2) are mutually independent and uniform.  Consequently,
\[
 \mathbb E[\sigma^m]=\frac{1+(-1)^m}{2}=\mathbf 1\{m\text{ is even}\},
 \qquad
 \mathbb E[(-1)^{\alpha_k s}]=\frac{1+(-1)^s}{2}=\mathbf 1\{s=0\}
 \quad(s\in\mathbb F_2).
\]
Taking expectations in the preceding product and using independence therefore gives
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[\prod_{r=1}^mW_{j_r}\right]
 =\mathbf 1\{m\text{ is even}\}
  \mathbf 1\!\left\{\bigoplus_{r=1}^m j_r=0\right\}
  (-1)^{\sum_{r=1}^m\phi_8(j_r)}.
\]
This is zero for odd (m), and for even (m) it is exactly the coefficient asserted in the lemma (and in (mathrm{def{:}fourth  ext{-}tensor  ext{-}certificate})).

For the stated fourth moment, (0\oplus1\oplus2\oplus3=0).  Moreover, from (phi_8(j)=j_0j_1+j_1j_2),
\[
 (\phi_8(0),\phi_8(1),\phi_8(2),\phi_8(3))=(0,0,0,1).
\]
The even-moment formula thus yields
\[
 \mathbb E[W_0W_1W_2W_3]=(-1)^{0+0+0+1}=-1.
\]

It remains to verify the finite covariance calculation rather than infer it from complementarity.  The phase-sign row and the three affine-mask rows are
\[
 b:=((-1)^{\phi_8(j)})_{j=0}^7=(+,+,+,-,+,+,-,+),
\]
\[
 r_0=(+,-,+,-,+,-,+,-),\qquad
 r_1=(+,+,-,-,+,+,-,-),\qquad
 r_2=(+,+,+,+,-,-,-,-).
\]
Hence the row indexed by (alpha=(alpha_0,alpha_1,alpha_2)) and (sigma=1) is the componentwise product
\[
 b\,r_0^{\alpha_0}r_1^{\alpha_1}r_2^{\alpha_2}.
\]
For (alpha=000,001,010,011,100,101,110,111), direct componentwise multiplication gives, in that order, precisely the eight (W)-rows displayed in (mathrm{def{:}l8  ext{-}golay  ext{-}audit}).  Applying the definition
\[
 C_{8,h}(w)=\sum_{t=1}^{8-h}w_tw_{t+h},\qquad h=1,2,3,
\]
with the harmless reindexing of the displayed block coordinates from (0,ldots,7) to (1,ldots,8), gives the corresponding exact list
\[
 \begin{split}
 c_{000}&=(-1,0,3),&c_{001}&=(1,0,-3),\\
 c_{010}&=(1,0,1),&c_{011}&=(-1,0,-1),\\
 c_{100}&=(1,0,-3),&c_{101}&=(-1,0,3),\\
 c_{110}&=(-1,0,-1),&c_{111}&=(1,0,1).
 \end{split}
\]
These sums are also the three rightmost columns of the displayed audit table.  Multiplication of an entire row by (sigma=-1) leaves every product (w_tw_{t+h}), and hence every (C_{8,h}), unchanged.  Since (alpha) is uniform on eight masks and independent of (sigma), the definition of (M_8) in (mathrm{def{:}block  ext{-}covariance  ext{-}objects}) gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 M_8
 &=\frac18\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbb F_2^3}c_\alpha c_\alpha^{\top}\\
 &=\frac18
 \begin{pmatrix}
 8&0&-8\\
 0&0&0\\
 -8&0&40
 \end{pmatrix}
 =\begin{pmatrix}
 1&0&-1\\
 0&0&0\\
 -1&0&5
 \end{pmatrix}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Finally, for (d=3), the same definition states (H_3=\operatorname{Diag}(1,2,3)).  Entrywise addition therefore yields
\[
 M_8+H_3=
 \begin{pmatrix}
 2&0&-1\\
 0&2&0\\
 -1&0&8
 \end{pmatrix},
\]
which proves every assertion.
